item.title: Qdrant .NET Client Adds gRPC Support and TLS Configuration
item.description:
Qdrant .NET Client Adds gRPC Support and TLS Configuration

A new .NET client library for Qdrant has been released, allowing .NET applications to connect to the vector database at http://localhost:6334 using gRPC.

🔍 Overview

  • Install the library with dotnet add package Qdrant.Client.
  • The client connects by default to Qdrant on http://localhost:6334.
  • Internally, the high‑level client relies on a low‑level gRPC client to communicate with Qdrant.

🧩 How it works

  • The client creates a channel via QdrantChannel.ForAddress, which is used by both QdrantClient("localhost") and the ClientConfiguration overloads.
  • When the channel is created, the client automatically adds a qdrant-dotnet/<version> token to the request User-Agent alongside the gRPC library token.
  • This token enables server‑side tooling to attribute traffic to the .NET client and its version.
  • On .NET Framework, where the underlying channel handler must be configured manually, the token is not added automatically.

⚙️ Configuration options

  • Additional constructor overloads give developers more control over gRPC client configuration.
  • TLS can be configured, validating the server certificate using its thumbprint, and API‑key authentication can be added.
  • .NET Framework has limited support for gRPC over HTTP/2, but support can be enabled by:
    • Referencing System.Net.Http.WinHttpHandler version 6.0.1 or later.
    • Configuring WinHttpHandler as the inner handler for GrpcChannelOptions.

🚀 Usage example 

1
2
3
4

await client.CreateCollectionAsync("my_collection", new VectorParams { Size = 100, Distance = Distance.Cosine });
// Query examples (illustrative):
// return the 5 closest points
// return the 5 closest points where rand_number >= 3

📡 Compatibility notes

  • On .NET Framework, manual configuration of the channel handler is required, and the automatic User-Agent token is not added.
  • The client works out‑of‑the‑box on platforms where gRPC over HTTP/2 is supported without additional handlers.

item.title: New Java Library for Qdrant Vector Search Engine Released
item.description:
New Java Library for Qdrant Vector Search Engine Released

A new Java library for the Qdrant vector search engine has been released, providing a high-level client with utility methods for interfacing with Qdrant. The library requires Java 8 or above and uses a low-level gRPC client internally to interact with Qdrant.

📦 Installation

To install the library, add the following lines to your build config file. Please ensure all necessary dependencies listed in the documentation are included in your project.

🛠️ How It Works

The client provides convenient methods and overloads for common operations, including:

  • Creating a new collection
  • Inserting vectors into a collection
  • Searching for similar vectors
  • Searching for similar vectors with filtering conditions

🔐 Configuration

Additional constructor overloads allow fine-grained control over the gRPC client configuration. For example, the following demonstrates how to configure a client to use TLS with certificate validation via the root CA and API key authentication.

🔄 Lifecycle Management

The client implements AutoCloseable, though it is typically created once and used for the application’s lifetime. When constructed by passing a ManagedChannel, the client does not shut down the channel on close by default. It can be configured to shut down the channel upon closing instead.

⏱️ Asynchronous Operations

All client methods return ListenableFuture<T>, enabling asynchronous workflows.

📚 Resources

Usage examples are available in the Qdrant documentation and API Reference.

#Java #Qdrant #VectorSearch #gRPC #ArtificialIntelligence

Source: qdrant/java-client

item.title: A2A Java SDK releases client and server support for agent communication
item.description:
A2A Java SDK releases client and server support for agent communication

A new Java library has been released to support the execution of agentic applications as Agent2Agent (A2A) servers. This multi-module Maven library provides both client and server capabilities, enabling A2A agent communication across JSON-RPC, gRPC, and REST transports.

🧩 How it works

The library facilitates agent-to-agent interaction by implementing the A2A Protocol. For gRPC support, the project copies the a2a.proto file from the A2A specification repository into the spec-grpc/ project. The java_package option is adjusted to target the org.a2aproject.sdk.grpc package. Developers can regenerate the gRPC classes by building the module with the command mvn clean install -Dskip.protobuf.generate=false.

⚙️ Key details

  • Language Requirement: Java 17 or later is required.
  • Transport Protocols: Supports JSON-RPC, gRPC, and REST.
  • Licensing: The project is licensed under the Apache 2.0 License.
  • Documentation: Full documentation is available at a2aproject.github.io/a2a-java.

🚀 Availability and Integrations

Developers can add the A2A Java SDK reference server for JSON-RPC to their Maven projects. The SDK includes examples for cross-language integration, such as a Java A2A server communicating with a Python client, and a Java A2A client communicating with a Python server.

Feature Details
OpenTelemetry Available as an optional add-on in the extras folder
JPA-backed task store Available as an optional add-on in the extras folder
Kafka-based replicated queue manager Available as an optional add-on in the extras folder
Vert.x and Android HTTP clients Available as optional add-ons in the extras folder

Integrations with Java runtimes are documented in the Server Integrations section of the reference materials.

#Java #AIagents #A2A #Maven #gRPC

Source: a2aproject/a2a-java

item.title: Go client released for Qdrant vector search engine
item.description:
Go client released for Qdrant vector search engine

The Go client for the Qdrant vector search engine has been released, making it easier for developers to integrate vector search capabilities into their Go applications. Internally, the high-level client uses a low-level gRPC client to interact with Qdrant, abstracting away the complexity of direct API calls. The client supports secure communication with TLS 1.3 as the minimum required version when UseTLS is enabled.

📦 Availability

The client can be installed using the Go package manager:

  • go get -u github.com/qdrant/go-client

🔐 Security

  • Uses TLS 1.3 as the minimum security version when UseTLS: true is set

🧩 Architecture

  • High-level client provides simplified API for common operations
  • Low-level gRPC client handles direct communication with Qdrant server

💡 Why it matters

This release enables Go developers to leverage Qdrant’s vector search capabilities without implementing low-level networking code, accelerating the development of AI and machine learning applications that require semantic search functionality.

#Go #Qdrant #VectorSearch #gRPC #TLS #AI

Source: qdrant/go-client

item.title: vLLM Open Data Hub Adapter Released on PyPi
item.description:
vLLM Open Data Hub Adapter Released on PyPi

A new adapter, vllm-tgis-adapter, has been made available on PyPi, facilitating the integration of vLLM with specific server infrastructure.

📦 Installation and Monitoring

The package is distributed via PyPi. The installation process includes an additional tool that assists in monitoring the underlying services:

  • Installing the adapter also installs a grpc healthcheck CLI.
  • This CLI can be used to monitor the status of the grpc server.

⚙️ Server Configuration

The adapter interacts with a gRPC server environment:

  • This will start serving a grpc server on port 8033.
  • This can be queried with grpcurl.

🐳 Container Image

An image for deployment is available at:

  • quay.io/opendatahub/vllm
  • This image is built from opendatahub-io/vllm’s Dockerfile.ubi.

🧪 Development and Testing Tools

The project utilizes specific tools for test automation and environment management:

  • Nox is used to manage test automation.
  • UV is used for venv management.
  • The standard vllm built requires an Nvidia GPU.
  • When this is not available, it is possible to compile vllm from source with CPU support.
  • This makes it possible to run the tests on most hardware.
  • Please note that the uv extra index url is required in order to install the torch CPU version.

#vLLM #Python #gRPC #DevTools #OpenDataHub

Source: opendatahub-io/vllm-tgis-adapter
